success_patterns: Keep the question’s specified measure attached to every almost-everywhere claim; a set that is null for ambient Lebesgue measure may still carry the relative probability measure used in the question.
Match the precise theorem criterion to the options, distinguishing a full convergence/divergence alternative from claims with extra conditions, modified series, or only one direction.

patch.reasoning: The skill already emphasizes exact theorem scope and distinguishing necessity from sufficiency, so those patterns need no duplicate rule. It does not explicitly warn that an almost-everywhere claim may use a measure supported on an ambient-null subset; preserving the stated reference measure is a useful general addition.

edits.content: For every almost-everywhere statement, identify and preserve the specified reference measure. A set may be null for ambient Lebesgue measure yet carry the probability measure used on a restricted locus; likewise, on a submanifold use the stated induced measure rather than silently switching to ambient measure.
